title: Review: Motion in electromagnetic fields

Terms and clues: D.3.5#xt2 term and clue written for the game; D.3.6#xt2 term and clue written for the game; D.3.2#xt1 term and clue written for the game; D.3.5#xt1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D.3#q03, D.3#q05, D.3#q10, D.3#q13, D.3#q16, D.3#q01, D.3#q04, D.3#q09, D.3#q12, D.3#q14, D.3#q02, D.3#q06. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Tesla
items.clue: The SI unit of B, equivalent to 1 N A⁻¹ m⁻¹.

items.label: Force per unit length
items.clue: The quantity μ₀I₁I₂/(2πr) for two long parallel wires, measured in N m⁻¹.

items.label: Circular motion
items.clue: Followed at constant speed by a charge travelling perpendicular to a uniform B; r = mv/qB.

items.label: Magnetic field strength
items.clue: The vector B: its size is F/(IL) for a straight current-carrying wire at right angles to it.

questions.stem: Two parallel plates, 2.0 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 500 V between them. An electron is released from rest at the negative plate and accelerates across the gap. What is its speed when it reaches the positive plate? Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.
questions.explanation: The work done by the field on the electron, eV, becomes kinetic energy: eV = ½m_ev², so v = √(2 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C × 500 V ÷ 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) = 1.3 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. The plate separation does not affect the final speed.

questions.stem: Positive ions of a single type, initially at rest, are accelerated through a potential difference of 1500 V. They then enter a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.25 T at right angles to their velocity, travel through a semicircle and strike a detector 6.3 cm from the point where they entered the field. What is the charge-to-mass ratio q/m of the ions?

options.text: 2.4 × 10⁷ C kg⁻¹
1.2 × 10⁷ C kg⁻¹
4.8 × 10³ C kg⁻¹
4.8 × 10⁷ C kg⁻¹

questions.explanation: The detector is one diameter from the entry point, so r = 3.15 cm = 0.0315 m. From qV = ½mv² and r = mv/(qB), q/m = 2V/(B²r²) = 2 × 1500 ÷ (0.25² × 0.0315²) = 4.8 × 10⁷ C kg⁻¹.

questions.stem: An electron moves towards the right of the page, in the plane of the page, through a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the electron at that instant?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the bottom of the page
Towards the left of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.explanation: The force is perpendicular to both the velocity (right) and the field (into the page), so it lies along the top–bottom line of the page. A positive charge would be pushed towards the top of the page; the electron is negative, so the force on it is towards the bottom.

questions.stem: A straight wire lies in the plane of the page and carries a current towards the right of the page. A uniform magnetic field in the plane of the page is directed towards the top of the page. What is the direction of the force on the wire?

options.text: Towards the top of the page
Towards the right of the page
Out of the plane of the page
Into the plane of the page

questions.explanation: The force is perpendicular to both the current (right) and the field (towards the top), so it is along the line into or out of the page. For a current to the right in a field towards the top of the page, it is out of the page.

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel copper wires are 5.0 cm apart in air. One carries a current of 2.0 A and the other a current of 6.0 A, in the same direction. Which statement about the magnetic forces between the wires is correct?

options.text: The wires push each other apart, as their currents are in the same direction.
Each wire is pulled towards the other by a force of the same magnitude.
Neither wire feels a force, as copper is not a magnetic material.
The 6.0 A wire pulls the 2.0 A wire harder than the 2.0 A wire pulls it.

questions.explanation: Each wire lies in the magnetic field of the other, and for currents in the same direction the force F = BIL on each points towards the other wire. The forces form a Newton's third law pair: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πr) is the same for both wires even though the currents differ.

questions.stem: An electron moves horizontally into the region between two horizontal parallel plates, midway between them and at right angles to the uniform electric field between the plates. It is deflected towards the positive plate. Gravity is negligible. Which describes the motion of the electron while it is between the plates?

options.text: A parabola: its horizontal velocity is constant as it accelerates towards the positive plate
A circular arc at constant speed, with the force at right angles to its velocity
A straight line at an angle, moving towards the positive plate at a steady velocity
A curve along which its horizontal velocity decreases as it is pulled sideways

questions.stem: A proton moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to its velocity. No other forces act on it. Which statement about the kinetic energy of the proton is correct?

options.text: It varies continuously around the circle, as the direction of the proton's velocity keeps changing.
It stays constant, because the magnetic force is perpendicular to its velocity.
It increases steadily, because the magnetic force accelerates the proton and so does work on it.
It decreases steadily, because the magnetic force acts against the proton's motion.

questions.stem: A proton moves at 3.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ in a uniform magnetic field of strength 40 mT. The velocity of the proton makes an angle of 25° with the direction of the field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on the proton? Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
questions.explanation: F = qvB sin θ with θ the angle between the velocity and the field: F = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C × 3.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ × 0.040 T × sin 25° = 8.1 × 10⁻¹⁵ N.

questions.stem: A straight wire 0.40 m long carries a current of 3.0 A. Only 0.25 m of the wire lies inside a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.080 T, and the wire makes an angle of 30° with the direction of the field. What is the magnitude of the force on the wire?
questions.explanation: F = BIL sin θ, with L the length inside the field and θ the angle between the wire and the field: F = 0.080 T × 3.0 A × 0.25 m × sin 30° = 3.0 × 10⁻² N.

questions.stem: Two long straight parallel wires in air are 4.0 cm apart and carry currents of 5.0 A and 8.0 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on a 1.5 m length of the wire carrying 8.0 A? Take μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹ for air.

Two horizontal parallel plates, 2.5 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 150 V between them. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of an electron between the plates? Gravity is negligible. Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

options.text: 1.1 × 10¹³ m s⁻²
2.6 × 10¹³ m s⁻²
6.6 × 10¹¹ m s⁻²
1.1 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻²

questions.stem: A proton moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to its velocity. A second proton moves at twice the speed of the first, perpendicular to the same field. Compared with the first proton, what are the radius of the second proton's circle and the time it takes to complete one revolution?

options.text: Radius halved; time for one revolution reduced to a quarter
Radius doubled; time for one revolution unchanged
Radius unchanged; time for one revolution halved
Radius doubled; time for one revolution halved as well

questions.explanation: From qvB = mv²/r, r = mv/(qB), so doubling v doubles r. The time for one revolution is T = 2πr/v = 2πm/(qB): the path is twice as long but covered at twice the speed, so T is unchanged.
